report_name: Google Disrupts 1.3M-Device XCPE Botnet, Bans Chinese Manufacturer

threat_actors.name: Videostrong Technology Co.
threat_actors.description: A China-based Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) that created and operated the XCPE botnet by pre-installing the malware in the firmware of its Android devices for financial gain through ad fraud and residential proxy services.

attack_patterns.name: Compromise Hardware Supply Chain
attack_patterns.description: Videostrong Technology Co. intentionally pre-installed the XCPE malware onto the firmware of its Android devices during the manufacturing process.

attack_patterns.name: System Firmware
attack_patterns.description: The XCPE malware was embedded in the device firmware, granting it system-level persistence that could survive factory resets.

attack_patterns.name: Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
attack_patterns.description: The XCPE botnet communicated with its command-and-control (C2) servers using web protocols to receive instructions and download additional payloads.

attack_patterns.name: Resource Hijacking
attack_patterns.description: Compromised devices in the XCPE botnet had their bandwidth and system resources hijacked to perform ad fraud and serve as proxy nodes.

attack_patterns.name: Proxy
attack_patterns.description: The XCPE botnet was used as a residential proxy service, allowing criminal affiliates to route their malicious traffic through the IP addresses of unsuspecting users.

malware.name: XCPE
malware.description: A malware embedded in the firmware of Android devices, creating a botnet of over 1.3 million devices used for ad fraud and as a residential proxy service.

identities.name: Linkfog
identities.description: A residential proxy-as-a-service network that affiliates of the XCPE botnet used to monetize access to the compromised devices.

identities.name: Honeygain
identities.description: A residential proxy-as-a-service network (mentioned as AppSalt/Honeygain) that affiliates of the XCPE botnet used to monetize access to the compromised devices.

identities.name: Traffmonetizer
identities.description: A residential proxy-as-a-service network that affiliates of the XCPE botnet used to monetize access to the compromised devices.

infrastructure.name: XCPE C2 Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: Command-and-control servers used by the XCPE botnet to manage compromised devices. This infrastructure was targeted for takedown by Google.

infrastructure.name: XCPE Botnet
infrastructure.description: A network of over 1.3 million compromised Android TV set-top boxes and other IoT devices controlled by the XCPE malware.

infrastructure.name: XCPE Residential Proxy Network
infrastructure.description: The network of compromised devices was sold as a residential proxy service to criminal affiliates, allowing them to obfuscate their traffic.

indicators.name: XCPE Botnet Affiliate Proxy Service DNS Query
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: XCPE Botnet Affiliate Proxy Service DNS Query
id: 2b1a8c3d-f4e5-4b6a-8d7c-9e0f1a2b3c4d
status: experimental
description: Detects DNS queries to known residential proxy services used by the XCPE botnet affiliates.
references:
  - https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/shutting-the-door-on-the-xcpe-botnet
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-03
tags:
  - attack.t1090
  - attack.command_and_control
level: high
logsource:
  category: dns_query
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    QueryName|contains:
      - 'linkfog.com'
      - 'honeygain.com'
      - 'traffmonetizer.com'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects DNS queries for domains associated with residential proxy services that were used to monetize the XCPE botnet.

indicators.name: Anomalous High-Bandwidth Outbound Traffic from IoT Device
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous High-Bandwidth Outbound Traffic from IoT Device
id: 5e4d3c2b-1a0f-4e9d-8c7b-6a5b4c3d2e1f
status: experimental
description: Detects sustained, high-bandwidth outbound traffic from IoT devices like set-top boxes, which could indicate their use as a proxy node in a botnet like XCPE.
references:
  - https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/shutting-the-door-on-the-xcpe-botnet
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-03
tags:
  - attack.t1496
  - attack.command_and_control
level: medium
logsource:
  category: firewall
detection:
  selection:
    # This is a generic rule. The source IP and byte threshold should be adapted to the specific environment.
    # Example: src_ip could be the IP range for IoT devices.
    src_ip: '192.168.1.0/24'
    sent_bytes|gt: 100000000 # 100 MB
  timeframe: 1h
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects sustained, high-bandwidth outbound traffic from set-top boxes or other IoT devices, which could indicate their use as a proxy node as seen with the XCPE botnet.
